div.head: Ps Cn for 15
div.ab: Si quis uim aliquam primariis foreste mee intulerit, si liberalis sit, amittat libertatem et omnia sua; si uillanus, abscindatur dextra.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 623 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: If anyone does any violence to the chief men of my forest, if he is a noble, let him lose his freedom and all his goods; if a villein, let his right hand be cut off.

note.seg: Vielleicht nicht ‘Gefängnis’ (s. d. Gl 6f. g), sondern ‘Verknechtung’ (s. d. Gl 12a). Sie übte Schottland 1080—90 an kriegsgefangenen Angelsachsen (Sym. Dunelm. 247); der strafrechtlich harte Verfasser entnahm sie gern dem Altertum. — Vielleicht ist eine Zeile übersprungen, und meinte Verf., den illiberalis zu verknechten, den liberalis aber mit Adelsverlust zu strafen, wie u. 22. 25

Perhaps not ‘imprisonment’ (see that word in Gl 6f. g) but ‘enslavement’ (see that word in Gl 12a). Scotland practised it in 1080—90 on Anglo-Saxon prisoners of war (Sym. Dunelm. 247); the author, harsh in penal matters, was glad to take it from antiquity. — Perhaps a line has been skipped, and the author meant to enslave the illiberalis but to punish the liberalis with loss of noble rank, as below 22. 25

S. Gl Hand 11d. f. Verf. übertreibt den Schutz für Königsbeamte im Anschluss an wirklichen Gerichtsfrieden (s. d. Gl 4) und Strafen für blutig (s. d. 5. 8) fechten in Gegenwart staatlicher Obrigkeit; s. Widerstand 1. 7

See Gl Hand 11d. f. The author exaggerates the protection of royal officials, following the real peace of the court (see that word in Gl 4) and the penalties for fighting to bloodshed (see that word 5. 8) in the presence of public authority; see Widerstand 1. 7
